findings.title: Denial cache defeats the newly-created-resource fix and blocks grants for 30s
findings.body: When a check is denied, Check writes a denial entry for (user, action, name, folder) with a 30s TTL, and every later Check returns deny from that entry before looking at permissions. Nothing invalidates the entry when permissions change. A user who checks a resource just before its permission row is visible (for example, a creator racing dashboard creation), or before being granted access, stays denied for up to 30s. This brings back the exact problem the PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Denial key uses raw subject UID and ambiguous concatenation
findings.body: The denial key is built from checkReq.UserUID, the raw subject string, which can be a numeric ID or a UID. The permission cache instead uses the resolved userIdentifiers.UID, so the two caches key the same user differently. The key also omits the identity type, so a user and an anonymous or service-account identity with the same ID would share denial entries. Finally, name and parent are joined with '_', which also appears in names, so different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key. Any of these collisions can deny the wrong subject or resource.

findings.title: Every cached deny now triggers a DB query, cache hits double-counted
findings.body: When cached permissions deny a request, Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which now always queries the DB. The singleflight cache-check was removed from it. So every first-time denied check hits the database. When the denial cache returns, permissionCacheUsage is incremented with the label "true". On the fallthrough path, the "false" label is incremented even when the cache was actually hit. Both make the cache metrics misleading.

findings.title: Denial test does not prove the cache bypass
findings.body: This test is meant to show that the denial cache short-circuits the permission check. However, it sets the permission cache to map{dash1: false}, which would deny the request anyway. The test therefore passes whether or not the denial cache works. It should set dash1 to true so that only the denial cache can explain the deny.
